scope: Top Eleven community-driven companion logic from forum + r/topeleven, prioritising Sep 2024-Sep 2026 and current 2026 reports.
policy: These rules rank plausible plans when private Nordeus effectiveness maths is unavailable. They are COMPANION LOGIC, never GAME FACT. Game legality/native semantics always override community claims.

decision_principles.rule: Score formation, tactics and Mentor as one coherent plan rather than independent picks.
decision_principles.reason: Current Mentor reports repeatedly depend on tactic family, while formation advice repeatedly changes passing/focus and defensive posture.

decision_principles.rule: Strongly reward central midfield parity/control; penalise being badly outnumbered in MC/DMC zones even when headline possession is acceptable.
decision_principles.reason: Repeated 2024-26 advice and match review identifies weak/empty midfield as a primary failure mode.

decision_principles.rule: Reward at least one DMC when the opponent uses AMC/central overloads; consider two DMCs against strong central/transition threats or when materially weaker.
decision_principles.reason: DMC screening is one of the most repeated community recommendations across current and recent posts.

decision_principles.rule: Attack the opponent's least-protected lane: reward flank focus against narrow/central-heavy shapes; reward central/AMC focus when there is no DMC/central screen.
decision_principles.reason: This is the most consistent counter principle across forum and Reddit, and aligns with game-authored Assistant Feedback semantics.

decision_principles.rule: Against equal/stronger teams, penalise overly attacking structures and reward defensive redundancy, DMC cover and coherent counter/transition outlets.
decision_principles.reason: Current successful stronger-opponent reports commonly add screening or lower structural risk rather than simply increasing attack.

decision_principles.rule: Short passing gains fit when the selected formation has close central support and aims to retain/control; mixed/long gains fit when bypassing a congested midfield or feeding a direct/aerial outlet.
decision_principles.reason: Repeated formation-specific advice and Target-Man reports point to system-dependent distribution rather than one global best passing style.

decision_principles.rule: Do not optimise possession percentage as the primary objective; use it only as one signal behind structural matchup and chance creation.
decision_principles.reason: Current 2026 example lost 0-3 despite 53% possession while being structurally overrun in central midfield.

decision_principles.rule: Keep both 3CB and back-four families in the candidate set. Prefer back four when opponent width/wide attackers demand explicit flank coverage; allow 3CB when midfield reinforcement and wide midfield/wingback support compensate.
decision_principles.reason: 2024-26 community evidence is genuinely split; a universal 3CB or back-four rule is not supported.

decision_principles.rule: Mentor score must be conditional on the chosen tactic/formation plan, not a standalone best-Mentor ranking.
decision_principles.reason: Current Mentor discussion consistently frames value around matching the active tactic family and halftime needs.

decision_principles.rule: Give Lewis Green a strong synergy bonus only when the plan intentionally creates wide/cross service and has an aerial/Target-Man outlet; do not rank him globally.
decision_principles.reason: Current player results closely match the extracted Wing/Crossing/Heading/Aerial Signature semantics.

decision_principles.rule: Give Cesc Fabregas a strong fit bonus to short/possession/combination plans and Ruben Herrera a strong fit bonus to counterattack/direct-transition plans; Jonas Braun gains value as a halftime adaptation option rather than a universal pre-match winner.
decision_principles.reason: Multiple current 2026 reports align directly with extracted Mentor tactic/signature families.

decision_principles.rule: Use ST Playstyle as a system-fit modifier: Target Man for cross/aerial service, Poacher when ST is primary scorer, False Nine when deeper linking/space creation supports other scorers.
decision_principles.reason: Current Reddit consensus aligns with current-client game-authored Playstyle semantics.

do_not_hardcode.reason: current 2026 back-four and alternative-system reports conflict

do_not_hardcode.claim: back four is universally best after the 2026 update
do_not_hardcode.reason: evidence is too sparse and anecdotal
current examples show possession can coexist with poor structural matchup/chance creation
community reports are inconsistent and game drain/risk context matters
current evidence strongly favours plan-specific Mentor alignment

implementation_boundary: Convert these qualitative rules into transparent companion score components only after defining visible reasons/diagnostics for each bonus or penalty. Do not claim the numeric companion score is Nordeus effectiveness.
